United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

title.narrative: Media Development and Media in Emergency, Multi-Donor Programme on Freedom of Expression and Safety of Journalists

description.narrative:
A series of activities will be tailored to (i) duty bearers, to improve legislative, financial or institutional frameworks related to media development, in particular with regard to the legal status and optimal functioning of Community Media, including those run by Indigenous Peoples’ Organizations, and (ii) rights holders, to reinforce their editorial and managerial capacities, increasing knowledge and raising awareness among media policy and decision makers on the importance of gender, disability and Indigenous peoples equality in media representation, content production and management practices. Efforts will be made to build advanced knowledge of media organizations on international normative instruments and professional standards. This also includes applying the media-related provisions contained in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD, 2006, Article 9 Accessibility, Article 21 Freedom of Expression and Opinion and Access to Information), the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP, 2007, Article 16 Indigenous Media), and the Global Action Plan of International Decade of Indigenous Languages 2022-2032 (Output 3 Media development). Synergies will be created with international cooperation mechanisms such as the International Decade of Indigenous Languages 2022-2032.
Member States will be supported in preparing for and responding to crises and emergencies through the media. This will be achieved primarily thanks to strengthened institutional capacity and practices of media for reporting solutions regarding the multiple crises on the rise globally, ranging from natural disasters exacerbated by climate change to human-caused disasters such as displacement and food crises, terrorism, and war. Media will be able to apply digital tools for news gathering and production and to safeguard journalistic standards and principles even in emergency situations. With enhanced access to public interest content and interaction through media throughout the crisis management cycle, from prevention and preparedness to response and recovery, people, in particular the most vulnerable, will be better equipped to make informed decisions and to prevent loss of life and livelihood.
Through better media practices in crisis preparedness and response, UNESCO will contribute to the implementation of relevant UN frameworks , including the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction and the Global Compact on Refugees.
